title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Environment Readiness
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding progress and infra readiness. Redwood team confirmed access status and next steps for VPC peering, IAM roles, and benchmark runs. Discussed initial latency/throughput numbers and tuning plan (quantization, batching, prefix cache). Action items assigned for benchmarks, security docs, and infra artifacts.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-29 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Priya Shah, Marcus Lee (Redwood) / Sara Gomez, Tom Reynolds, Aisha Khan (NexaHealth)

[00:00] Priya Shah: hey everybody, thanks for joining. how's the timing? we have about 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:08] Sara Gomez: hi, sara here from nexa, i've got tom and aisha on as well. we're good.
[00:12] Tom Reynolds: tom here, infra lead.
[00:15] Aisha Khan: aisha, ml eng, hi.
[00:17] Priya Shah: awesome. marcus from our side as well, do you want to kick off with infra access status?
[00:22] Marcus Lee: yeah, sure. so last week we asked for VPC peering details, a service account with iam permissions for provisioning, and sample dataset access. tom, where are we on those?
[00:34] Tom Reynolds: we created the peering request this morning, but there's a network review queue. security wants to validate routing tables and NACLs. i put the ticket in for the peering acceptance, should be 24-48 hours. service account - done, we added the role redwood-poc-provisioner but i'm not 100% sure on the fine-grained perms, i'll send the exact policy after this call. dataset - sara will share the obfuscated sample set.
[00:52] Priya Shah: perfect, thanks. sara did you already obfuscate the PII fields?
[00:55] Sara Gomez: yes, we removed direct identifiers, kept some synthetic PHI to test redaction. there's a note in the doc about fields to mask but it's not 100% exhaustive, so we'd appreciate any feedback.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: that helps. for the initial run we'll use hosted test endpoints on our sandbox, then move the heavy benchmarks to your dedicated hosts when peering is live. small heads-up: we saw slight tokenization differences between the sample preprocessor you shared and our tokenizer - might cause a couple of tokens more per doc, so perf numbers could be off by 5-8%.
[01:28] Aisha Khan: oh interesting, do you mean like whitespace handling? we use the standard byte-level tokenizer from the upstream model.
[01:33] Marcus Lee: yeah, some whitespace normalization and newline splits. we'll send a quick script to mirror your pipeline so numbers align.
[01:38] Priya Shah: ok on the pipeline script, we'll attach that to the slack thread later today.
[01:42] [02:00] (brief mutter, inaudible)
[02:10] Priya Shah: moving on - results review. marcus, can you summarize the initial latency/throughput run you did yesterday on the small sample in our sandbox?
[02:18] Marcus Lee: sure. ran sequence of 512 tokens for 1000 requests with concurrency of 8 - average p95 latency ~220ms on g5-like instance emulation, token generation rate roughly 70 tokens/sec, throughput around 560 requests/hour under that workload. note these were unquantized fp16 runs. when we tried 4-bit quantization locally, p95 increased slightly to ~240ms but cost per token dropped ~45%.
[02:44] Sara Gomez: 220ms p95 is within our soft goal but our product team is looking for sub-200 if possible during peak. that's our ask.
[02:52] Marcus Lee: understood. there are levers: batching, KV/prefix cache, kernel selection for longer sequences. also if you move to dedicated reserved gpus we can tune kernel params and reduce context-switch overhead which usually gets us under 200 for this profile.
[03:10] Tom Reynolds: when you say dedicated, are there differences in the networking path that could change latency? we need an SLA on p95 to present to ops.
[03:18] Priya Shah: good question. dedicated will often be colocated and the serving path shorter; also no multi-tenant scheduler pause. we can provide SLA targets in the dedicated offering, and we'll include expected network hop counts for the peered path. we'll follow up with an ops doc.
[03:33] Aisha Khan: any noise from KV cache warm-up? we saw some variability in earlier runs.
[03:37] Marcus Lee: yes, warm-up matters. with persistent KV cache and sticky routing during a session, we saw p95 drop by ~30ms after warm cache. for chat-like workloads it's important to keep sessions pinned.
[03:48] [03:55] (crosstalk)
[04:00] Sara Gomez: security - we need SOC 2 attestations and encryption at rest with KMS. are those already in place for the hosted sandbox?
[04:07] Priya Shah: for hosted sandbox we use envelope encryption with KMS and logs are accessible via the console with RBAC. for dedicated/private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs. i'll share the security pack — priya to send security docs.
[04:20] Marcus Lee: and one note, for private deployments we can run inside your VPC with an optional on-prem pack if ops requires air gap.
[04:27] Tom Reynolds: good. regarding IAM perms, we prefer least privilege. can you share a minimal role spec for the provisioner?
[04:33] Marcus Lee: yes i'll post a minimal policy - includes instance attach, SSM for debug (if approved), and read access to S3 buckets for dataset pulls.
[04:42] [05:00] (short pause)
[05:10] Priya Shah: next, tuning plan. marcus suggested quant + batching + prefix caching. what order do we want to try?
[05:17] Marcus Lee: i'd recommend: 1) align tokenization and pipeline (so numbers match), 2) run baseline on your peered setup, 3) evaluate 4-bit quant with quality checks on the small eval set, 4) enable batching and adjust batch window to meet latency targets, 5) enable KV/prefix cache and run warmup before stress tests.
[05:36] Aisha Khan: for quality checks, what metrics do you propose? rouge/bleu? we have domain-specific evaluation for PHI extraction accuracy.
[05:44] Marcus Lee: for generation quality we'll surface pairwise similarity, factuality checks, and your PHI extraction accuracy. we can plug your eval harness into our rollout so regressions alert automatically.
[05:55] Sara Gomez: excellent. timeline wise, product wants a decision on dedicated vs hosted by mid-june to lock budget.
[06:02] Priya Shah: understood — we'll prioritize a benchmark on peered infra next week so you have a better datapoint.
[06:08] Tom Reynolds: one blocker: our security team asked for audit log schema and retention policy before approving peering. do you have that?
[06:16] Priya Shah: yes, i'll attach the audit schema - includes request_id, token_count, model_version, user_id (hashed), region, timestamp. retention options are 30/90/365 days — we can align to your compliance needs.
[06:30] [06:40] (ambient noise)
[06:45] Marcus Lee: also ran into one oddity: we saw a small memory spike on long sequences when using a specific attention kernel; we'll test alternative kernels and update the notes.
[06:56] Aisha Khan: ok please call that out in the benchmark sheet, with config flags.
[06:59] Marcus Lee: will do.
[07:05] Priya Shah: recap and next steps: we'll send the pipeline tokenizer script; marcus to post minimal iam policy and benchmark config; tom to confirm peering ticket status and share route tables; sara to share obfuscated sample and eval harness; redwood to run peered benchmark next week and share results.
[07:22] Sara Gomez: sounds good. can you also include a cost estimate for dedicated per-month?
[07:27] Priya Shah: yes we'll include a cost range and the tradeoffs (latency vs cost).
[07:32] Tom Reynolds: timeline for those artifacts?
[07:35] Priya Shah: i'll send security pack and SOW draft by 2026-06-02; marcus will post iam and benchmark configs by 2026-06-01; we'll aim to run peered benchmark the week of 2026-06-01 and deliver results by 2026-06-04.
[07:50] (final quick questions)
[07:55] Aisha Khan: one more - do you support custom quant recipes? like Q/KV asymmetric quantization?
[07:59] Marcus Lee: we have some supported quant profiles and can test custom recipes during the POC, but for production we recommend validated profiles. we'll test your recipe if you share the config.
[08:10] Priya Shah: great. ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in slack and drop the docs. talk soon.

(End of transcript)
